multiRename.title: Multi-rename

@multiRename.title.description: Title of the Multi-Rename Tool sheet (Ctrl+M), which renames many files at once with a name mask, like Total Commander's tool of the same name.

@multiRename.nameMask.description: Label of the field holding the rename mask for the file name: plain text plus placeholders in brackets such as [N] (old name) or [C] (counter).

@multiRename.extensionMask.description: Label of the field holding the rename mask for the file extension, kept separate so a typo can't break the file type. [E] keeps the old extension.

@multiRename.insertPlaceholder.description: Accessible name of the row of buttons that insert a placeholder such as [N] or [C] into the name mask at the caret.

@multiRename.search.description: Label of the search field of the rename tool's search & replace. Supports * and ? wildcards and a|b|c lists.

@multiRename.replace.description: Label of the replacement field of the rename tool's search & replace. With a list search, x|y|z pairs up with it.

@multiRename.caseSensitive.description: Search & replace option: only match the same uppercase/lowercase letters.

@multiRename.firstOnly.description: Search & replace option: replace only the first match in each name, not all of them.

@multiRename.includeExtension.description: Search & replace option: also search and replace in the file extension.

@multiRename.regex.description: Search & replace option: the search is a regular expression; $1, $2 in the replacement insert its groups.

@multiRename.substitute.description: Search & replace option: when the search matches, the whole name becomes the replacement (Total Commander's "Subst.").

@multiRename.case.description: Label of the menu that changes the letter case of the new names, applied after search & replace.

@multiRename.case.unchanged.description: Letter-case menu option: keep the letter case as it is.

@multiRename.case.lower.description: Letter-case menu option: all letters lowercase. Written in lowercase on purpose, to show the result.

@multiRename.case.upper.description: Letter-case menu option: all letters uppercase. Written in uppercase on purpose, to show the result.

@multiRename.case.firstUpper.description: Letter-case menu option: the first letter of the name uppercase, the rest lowercase.

@multiRename.case.words.description: Letter-case menu option: the first letter of every word uppercase, the rest lowercase. Written that way on purpose, to show the result.

@multiRename.removeDiacritics.description: Option: turn letters with accents and other diacritics into plain letters (á becomes a, ž becomes z, ß becomes ss), in every language.

@multiRename.counterStart.description: Label of the number the counter placeholder [C] starts at.

@multiRename.counterStep.description: Label of the amount the counter placeholder [C] goes up (or down, when negative) per file.

@multiRename.counterDigits.description: Label of how many digits the counter placeholder [C] has; shorter numbers get leading zeros.

@multiRename.presets.description: Label of the menu of saved rename settings (presets) to load.

@multiRename.presetPlaceholder.description: Placeholder of the preset menu before one is chosen.

@multiRename.preset.default.description: Built-in preset that resets every setting, so all names stay as they are (Total Commander's <Default>).

@multiRename.preset.removeDiacritics.description: Built-in preset that keeps names as they are but removes diacritics (á becomes a, ž becomes z).

@multiRename.presetName.description: Label of the field where the user names the current settings to save them as a preset.

@multiRename.savePreset.description: Button that saves the current rename settings under the name in the Preset name field; an existing preset with that name is replaced.

@multiRename.deletePreset.description: Button that deletes the chosen saved preset.

@multiRename.preview.description: Accessible name of the table that previews every file's old and new name.

@multiRename.oldName.description: Preview table column: the file's current name.

@multiRename.newName.description: Preview table column: the name the file will get.

@multiRename.statusColumn.description: Header of the preview table's status column. Each row says whether the file will be renamed (ready), stays as it is (unchanged), or has a problem and why (invalid name, duplicate, name taken).

@multiRename.status.unchanged.description: Preview note: the new name is the same as the old one, so the file is left alone.

@multiRename.status.duplicate.description: Preview note: another file in this batch would get the same new name, so neither is renamed.

@multiRename.status.targetExists.description: Preview note: a file that stays in the folder already has this name.

@multiRename.status.invalidName.description: Preview note: the new name can't be a file name (empty, too long, or "." / "..").

@multiRename.status.disallowedCharacter.description: Preview note: the new name contains a character file names can't have, such as a slash. {character} is that character.

multiRename.error.unclosed: A placeholder is missing its closing “]”

@multiRename.error.unclosed.description: Shown when a mask has a [ without a matching ].

@multiRename.error.unknown.description: Shown when a mask has a placeholder that doesn't exist. {placeholder} is what's between the brackets.

@multiRename.error.badRegex.description: Shown when the search is a regular expression that can't be parsed.

multiRename.error.gone: This folder isn’t open any more. Close Multi-rename and open it again.

@multiRename.error.gone.description: Shown when the pane the tool renames in moved to another folder.

multiRename.error.nothingToRename: Nothing to rename: every new name is the same as the old one or has a problem

@multiRename.error.nothingToRename.description: Shown when Rename is pressed but no file is ready to be renamed.

multiRename.error.notConnected: This location isn’t connected right now

@multiRename.error.notConnected.description: Shown when the drive or server of the folder is no longer connected.

multiRename.error.couldntStart: Couldn’t start renaming. Try again in a moment.

@multiRename.error.couldntStart.description: Shown when the rename couldn't start (the rename queue refused it, or something went wrong inside Cmdr). Nothing was renamed.

multiRename.error.timedOut: That took too long, so Cmdr stopped waiting. Try again, or select fewer files.

@multiRename.error.timedOut.description: Shown under the Multi-rename preview when working out the new names, or getting the rename ready after Start, took longer than Cmdr waits. Nothing was renamed. 'Cmdr' is the app name; keep it untranslated.

multiRename.counts: {ready, plural, one {# to rename} other {# to rename}} · {unchanged, plural, one {# unchanged} other {# unchanged}} · {problems, plural, one {# problem} other {# problems}}

@multiRename.counts.description: Footer summary of the preview: how many files will be renamed, how many keep their name, and how many have a problem.

@multiRename.cancel.description: Button that closes the tool without renaming.

@multiRename.rename.description: Primary button that renames the files that are ready. {count} is how many.

multiRename.started: {count, plural, one {Renaming # file} other {Renaming # files}}. You can roll it back from the operation log.

@multiRename.started.description: Toast after Rename starts. {count} is how many files. The operation log is the window listing past operations, where Undo is. "Roll back" is the button's name in the operation log (operationLog.dialog.rollBack): use the same words.

multiRename.error.previewOutOfDate: The folder changed since the preview. Check the new preview, then rename again.

@multiRename.error.previewOutOfDate.description: Shown when Rename is pressed but files in the folder changed after the preview was shown, so nothing was renamed and the preview is refreshed.

multiRename.error.readOnly: This folder can’t be renamed in: it’s inside an archive or another read-only place

@multiRename.error.readOnly.description: Shown when Rename is pressed in a folder that can't be changed, such as the inside of a zip archive.

@multiRename.status.missing.description: Preview note: a file the user picked for renaming was deleted or moved out of the folder while the tool was open, so it can't be renamed.

multiRename.selectionChanged: The folder changed while Multi-rename was opening. Check your selection, then try again.

@multiRename.selectionChanged.description: Warning toast when ⌃M (Multi-rename) didn't open because files appeared or disappeared in the folder at that moment, so the selected rows may no longer be the files the user picked. Nothing was renamed.

multiRename.swapsSkipped: {count, plural, one {Skipped # rename that swaps names} other {Skipped # renames that swap names}}. Rename those files one at a time.

@multiRename.swapsSkipped.description: Warning toast after Rename starts on cloud storage (S3), when some renames swap names with each other (for example a → b and b → a). On S3, renaming a folder copies everything inside it, and copying one folder onto another that is still there would mix their contents, so those renames were skipped and the files kept their names. {count} is how many (always 2 or more). Match the wording of askCmdr.renameUndo.swapsSkipped.

@multiRename.archiveTitle.description: Alert title when ⌃M (Multi-rename) is pressed while browsing inside a zip archive. Cmdr can rename files in a zip one by one, but the Multi-rename tool only works in folders on a drive. "Multi-rename" is the tool’s name; match multiRename.title.

multiRename.archiveMessage: To rename files in this zip, rename them one at a time.

@multiRename.archiveMessage.description: Alert body under multiRename.archiveTitle. Points the user to renaming files inside the zip one by one (the regular single-file rename), which does work there.
